**Analysis**

- **step_01**: The group's event volume is essentially flat across the whole interval (~65–130 events per 3000-unit bin, no burst), so total volume alone cannot explain anything — a confounder control on activity level.
- **step_02**: Each group member has ~90 events over ~30–33 distinct partners across [2551, 32551], i.e. very little repeat contact per partner (≈3 events/partner).
- **step_03–step_08**: Tracking a representative member (214) in consecutive 5000-unit windows: 30 distinct partners in [2551, 7550], then **0, 0, 1, 0, 0** partners in all later windows. Its entire partner set (30 of its 31 lifetime partners) is confined to a single 5000-unit block and is then completely abandoned; the only later contact (1714) is not in the earlier set.

So for the candidate change point ≈7550 with a 5000 half-window, the before-set (30 nodes) and after-set (∅/{1714}) are disjoint → Jaccard overlap ≈ 0, dissimilarity ≈ 1.0, far above the 0.6 threshold. The flat aggregate volume (step_01) rules out "the group simply got busier/quieter", and the low per-partner repeat rate (step_02) rules out a popularity/hub artifact: the partner identities genuinely turn over as blocks rather than drifting gradually while old ties persist.

Caveat: the partner-set tracing was done on one representative member, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
